scenarios.final_decision_record:
# Design record: ledger export

## Scope and provenance

Unadopted working revision 5 of fixture ChatGPT draft revision 1. Originals remain
in [supplied/original](../../supplied/original/); edits belong in `drafts/current`.
This continuation applies explicit simulated answers to Q4, Q5 and Q6, retaining
all earlier answers and terminology, then records the user's additional explicit
material deferrals. Detailed review remains focused on retention and recovery;
other scope remains explicitly unreviewed. The user has now explicitly confirmed
summary retention-recovery-r5 after reading its actual section, without answering the
deferred design branches or changing any requirement. Authored groups remain single-file, then batch/resume. This record contains
fixture design answers, not acceptance of skill implementation or product execution.

## Decisions

| Decision | Requirement/acceptance | Status and actual answer | Rationale/consequences | Depends on / affected artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 Destination consent | RFC AC01 | Settled, revised in revision 2: “instead of refusing an existing destination, allow replacing it after an explicit per-command confirmation” | Supersedes the earlier refusal policy for the single-file destination. Absence, rejection or silence is not confirmation. Prior confirmation cannot authorize a later command. D8 now requires preserving the prior destination on every failed replacement. | Reopens affected confirmation and replacement safety; RFC, DRAFT-0001, single-file milestone, closeout |
| D2 Bounded files | RFC AC02; unchanged goals | Settled in supplied history: at most 100 data rows and 10 MiB | Exact bounds retained; no new answer inferred | RFC, cards and both milestone exits |
| D3 Job timeout | RFC AC01/AC02 | Settled in supplied history: 30 seconds | Exact proposed default retained; observed module declares 45 seconds and does not enforce a timeout. Full-input verification is not permission to extend the job limit. | RFC, cards and milestones |
| D4 Resume identity mismatch | RFC AC03 | Settled in supplied history: refuse mismatched input | Avoid duplicate/wrong output; D6 now settles verification by complete-input contents | Batch/resume and closeout |
| D5 Retention duration / Q1 | RFC AC04/AC05 | Settled answer: “retain completed files for 7 days” | Duration and operator ownership are settled. D10 now starts it at each file's first successful completion without resume resets; checkpoint age eligibility remains open in D12. | D7, D10, D11 and D12; both implementation cards and milestones |
| D6 Identity verification / Q2 | RFC AC03 | Settled explicit simulated answer: “use a digest of the complete input contents” | Compare the resumed input against the recorded complete-input digest before producing resumed output. Filename/size alone is insufficient. Digest algorithm and checkpoint internals remain optional detail. | RFC, DRAFT-0002, batch-resume exit and closeout |
| D7 Retention ownership / Q3 | RFC AC04/AC05 | Settled explicit simulated answer: “the operator owns retention and cleanup; export/resume commands must not automatically delete completed files” | A retention deadline does not authorize command cleanup. Preserve completed files from automatic retention deletion; D1's explicitly confirmed replacement remains a separate operator action. No cleanup service or command is introduced. | RFC, both implementation cards, both milestone exits, closeout; cleanup ownership remains settled |
| D8 Failed confirmed replacement / Q4 | RFC AC01 | Settled explicit simulated answer: preserve the previous destination until a complete replacement is available; interruption, a size/time limit or other replacement failure leaves it intact | Failed replacement must not truncate, remove or partially replace the prior destination; successful publication may replace it after per-command confirmation. Commit/staging mechanics are not prescribed. | RFC, DRAFT-0001, single-file exit and closeout |
| D9 Domain terminology | RFC terminology; pack-local glossary | Settled explicit simulated answer: “Keep Account as the ledger concept and call the produced artifact an export file” | No one-file/one-account assumption. No live glossary adoption is implied. | RFC, glossary, cards and question wording |
| D10 Retention clock / Q5 | RFC AC04/AC05 | Settled explicit simulated answer: the operator's seven days begin at each export file's first successful completion; later resume must not reset that start | Same per-file rule applies to single-file and batch output, including an unfinished batch. No automatic deletion follows from reaching the date. | RFC, both implementation cards, both exits and closeout |
| D11 Missing completed output / Q6 | RFC AC03/AC05 | Settled explicit simulated answer: stop with a clear missing-output error, preserve existing files and recorded completed progress, and do not automatically regenerate missing output | A checkpoint offset is not proof that recorded output remains available; respect operator cleanup and retain the recovery record for deliberate recovery. | RFC, DRAFT-0002, batch-resume exit and closeout |
| D12 Checkpoint age eligibility / Q7 | RFC AC05 | Explicitly deferred, material; no actual eligibility answer. The user assigned age-based checkpoint eligibility to later design work and understands affected scope remains unready. | Neither expiry nor indefinite resume is selected. The previous no-age-only-expiry recommendation remains unaccepted. | Batch recovery unready for this branch; RFC/card/plan/closeout carry the deferral |
| D13 Untrusted recovery data / Q8 | RFC AC03 | Explicitly deferred, material; no repair/refusal answer. The user deferred changed completed output and corrupt recovery-record branches to later design work. | Missing/unreadable/corrupt record cases grouped in Q8 remain unresolved; Q6 only settles missing completed output. No error/repair mechanism is chosen. | Batch recovery unready for this branch; RFC/card/plan/closeout carry the deferral |
| D14 Destination collision/race / Q9 and related race branch | RFC AC01/AC03 | Explicitly deferred, material; no collision/race answer. The user assigned destination collision/race branches to later design work. | No refusal, replacement, concurrency or ownership-resolution policy is selected for unrelated batch files or destination changes during confirmation/publication. D1/D8 remain settled for the defined single-file behavior. | Affected single-file destination-race and batch collision/race scope remain unready; RFC/cards/plan/closeout carry the deferral |

## Grounding and language

[ledger.py](../../ledger.py) opens the destination with mode `w`, writes the `account`
and `amount` columns and declares `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 45`. It has no batch,
resume, retention or confirmation path, and its export function does not enforce the
proposed row, size or timeout bounds. These are observed facts; the 30-second proposal
is unchanged. The supplied ownership refusal was a proposal, not current behavior.

The fixture glossary defines an account as a named grouping of ledger entries.
The resumed user explicitly retained that concept and chose “export file” for the
produced CSV. The [pack-local glossary](GLOSSARY.md) reflects that answer; no
one-file/one-account requirement is inferred, and no live glossary was changed.

## Interrupted round and actual continuation

- Q1 was explicitly answered as **7 days** in revision 2; duration remains settled.
- Q2 and Q3 were initially unanswered, then explicitly settled in revision 3 as
  complete-input contents digest and operator-owned retention/cleanup with no
  automatic deletion of completed files by export/resume commands.
- Q4 was deliberately unanswered through revision 3. It is now explicitly answered:
  preserve the previous destination until a complete replacement is available;
  interruption, a size/time limit or any other replacement failure leaves it intact.
- Q5 is now explicitly answered: each file's first successful completion starts the
  operator's seven days, and later resume must not reset that start.
- Q6 is now explicitly answered: missing checkpointed completed output causes a clear
  error while preserving existing files and recorded completed progress; no automatic
  regeneration is allowed.
- The additional simulated user scope decision explicitly defers age-based checkpoint
  eligibility, destination collision/race, changed completed output and corrupt
  recovery-record branches for later design work. The user understands these are
  material, leave affected scope unready, and are not a waiver or whole-pack readiness.
- Account/export-file terminology and D1–D4 remain unchanged. That deferral message
  explicitly does **not** confirm a summary/version that had not yet been presented.
  The subsequent exact confirmation of the presented revision-5 summary is recorded
  below; the earlier deferral message itself was not treated as confirmation.

## Deferred question record for later design work

Q7–Q9 retain the actual questions previously prepared, now explicitly deferred by
user scope decision. They are not the active frontier and require no answer in this
focused round. They remain material/unanswered, with affected scope unready. Their
recommendations are preserved as proposals only; none is accepted by the deferral.

**Q7 — May resume continue after the seven days if input, completed output and
  recovery data are still valid?**
For example, a batch is interrupted and the operator keeps every completed file for
10 days. Recommendation: do not expire its checkpoint merely because it is old;
retention remains the operator's policy, with normal recovery validation still required.

- **No age-only expiry (recommended):** Intact retained output remains resumable;
  missing output still stops under Q6, and cleanup remains the operator's choice.
- **Expire resume eligibility after seven days:** Require a fresh export after the
  retention deadline even if files remain; the checkpoint deadline must then be defined
  consistently for batches containing files completed at different times.

**Q8 — If a checkpoint is missing/corrupt or a completed file still exists but has
  changed, must resume stop, or may it offer explicit repair?**
Recommendation: stop with a clear recovery-data error, leave files and available
recorded progress unchanged, and require operator recovery. Q6 already settles the
separate missing-completed-file case; this question does not reopen it.

- **Stop and preserve (recommended):** Do not guess an offset or overwrite changed
  output; restoring a trustworthy recovery basis is an operator action.
- **Offer confirmed repair:** Add an explicitly confirmed reconstruction/repair path
  for damaged records or changed output; its validation and ownership contract would
  need a later dependent round. This does not permit automatic regeneration under Q6.

**Q9 — If the next numbered batch path contains an unrelated file, should batch or
  resume refuse, or allow explicitly confirmed replacement?**
Recommendation: refuse with a collision error while preserving that file, existing
completed output and recorded progress. Normal resume can still replace a proven
partial file belonging to its own interrupted run, as already proposed.

- **Refuse unrelated collisions (recommended):** Preserve output ownership; the
  operator can move the unrelated file or select a fresh batch directory.
- **Permit confirmed replacement:** Extend D1's per-command confirmation and D8's
  preservation-on-failure policy to that batch collision; this expands replacement
  behavior beyond the currently settled single-file scope.

## Remaining recovery branches and explicit deferrals

Q4–Q6 are settled by actual answers. The user's additional scope decision is: defer
“age-based checkpoint eligibility, destination collision/race, changed completed output
and corrupt recovery-record branches” for later design work, acknowledging that these
are material and their affected scope remains unready. This is an explicit deferral,
not a selected behavior, readiness waiver, acceptance evidence or whole-pack claim.

Consequences: AC05 remains unready for checkpoint-age behavior; AC03 remains unready
for changed output, untrusted recovery records and unrelated batch collision/race;
AC01's destination-race branch also remains unready. Existing settled mismatch refusal,
missing-output refusal/progress preservation and replacement-failure preservation
remain in force for their defined cases. No deferred branch is resolved by analogy.
The Q8 record-integrity group includes its already recorded missing/unreadable/corrupt
checkpoint cases; these remain unresolved for later design. The pre-existing single-
file row-bound discrepancy is retained separately as unreviewed, with full-scope
readiness unresolved.

Existing AC03 requires no duplicate entries after interruption, including a crash
after a file completes but before its offset is recorded. Partial files are excluded
from completed offsets. Full-input digest mismatch is refused without changing
completed files, and verification respects the existing 30-second job limit.
Exact transactional/checkpoint/staging mechanics, class/module structure and hash
algorithm remain optional internal design deferred under the observable constraints.
No implementation mechanism is imposed as an authoring/confirmation prerequisite.
General concurrent-writer support beyond the material destination-race deferral and
other unrelated scope remain unreviewed; no support or exclusion is adopted here.

## Readiness and coverage

Structural validity: `python3 -B` with the discovered implement-rfc offline
`examples/milestone-plans/validate.py` passed the final revision-5 JSON normally and
with `--render` (exit 0). Renderer stdout regenerated `MILESTONES.md`; the final
[receipt](checks/plan-validation-r5.json) records exact commands/results and the plan
SHA256. Earlier receipts are preserved. No unchanged plan check was repeated solely
for confirmation. Offline passes do not resolve live references, prove semantic
adequacy or supply implementation acceptance evidence. Defined criteria remain assigned
to the original plan groups; complete decomposition does not settle deferred material design.

Design readiness: the reviewed decisions are defined, and the user's material deferrals
are explicit with their consequences understood. Affected destination-race, checkpoint-
age, collision and recovery-data-integrity scope remains unready. Other scope, the
row-bound discrepancy and general concurrency remain unreviewed. No full milestone or
full pack is declared ready. Exact scoped synthetic confirmation is now recorded below.
Review coverage: retention duration/ownership/clock, missing-output recovery,
complete-input identity, interruption/offset recovery, replacement consent/failure,
terminology, plus identification and explicit deferral of the named material branches.
Execution eligibility is unevaluated: no live mappings, mandate, baseline, card claims
or implementation acceptance evidence is established by drafting checks or confirmation.

## Shared understanding and confirmation

Summary ID: **retention-recovery-r5**. Scope: the reviewed retention/recovery decisions
and their explicit deferrals in working revision 5, retaining supplied numeric bounds
and authored grouping. Other design scope is explicitly unreviewed.

1. The operator owns seven-day retention and cleanup, starting at each export file's

# Missing-companion tabletop result

Candidate: `39f02b7c654699e76233b8cfe6f966d915ca74b9`.

Result: useful independent grounding completed; complete RFC grilling and artifact synchronization remain pending. No answers or confirmation were fabricated.

## Actions and capability boundary

- Read this fixture's `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `ledger.py`, and the supplied working pack under `drafts/current/`.
- Used the discovered `grill-rfc` and `grill-me` guidance. The complete isolated inventory cannot resolve `author-rfc` or `implement-rfc`; no ambient or sibling copy of either absent capability was accessed.
- The candidate comparison `git diff --exit-code 39f02b7c654699e76233b8cfe6f966d915ca74b9 -- skills/grill-rfc/SKILL.md skills/grill-me/SKILL.md` returned exit 0. Although the canonical checkout HEAD is `d9a7cbace49d783c7dc5fda7ea5dbb31b72bc0dd`, the two skill files read match the requested candidate.
- Preserved the unadopted revision-1 pack, supplied decisions and two authored outcomes (`single-file`, then `batch-resume`). Did not revise RFCs, cards, the canonical plan or generated milestone view without the artifact-owning companion.
- Executed a bounded baseline probe using a temporary directory inside this fixture; removed its temporary CSV when the probe finished. Saved separate grounding evidence, without product implementation.

`author-rfc` is needed for the complete artifact contract, provenance handling and coordinated changes across RFC acceptance, decisions, cards, plan JSON and generated view. `implement-rfc` is needed for the companion's portable plan-kit workflow and its validation surfaces. A supplied schema file does not resolve either missing skill. Their portions remain pending.

## Observed facts and actual checks

`ledger.export` opens its destination in write mode. An execution probe replaced an existing sentinel file with the expected `account,amount` CSV and passed. The module declares `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 45`; inspection shows `export` does not enforce that timeout. The module's only top-level function is `export`, with no CLI, batch or resume definition. Thus the proposed refusal of existing destinations, 30-second timeout, CLI, bounds and recovery are proposed changes, not existing implementation behavior.

Both current plan JSON and supplied schema JSON parsed successfully. The plan assigns AC01 to `single-file`, and AC02/AC03 to `batch-resume` with a dependency on `single-file`. This records observed structure only. Schema validation was not run because `jsonschema` is unavailable; nothing was installed. The unavailable implement-rfc kit, reference resolution, semantic coverage, live selectors and execution eligibility were not verified.

SHA-256 checks confirmed that all read fixture instructions, glossary, source and working-pack files were unchanged during the grounding probe. The supplied originals were never modified or used as replacement outputs. There were no commits, pushes, installations, live selections, publication or source changes.

## Pending frontier questions for simulated replies

The following three questions have settled factual prerequisites. Their recommendations remain unaccepted. Return explicit simulated answers to the coordinator; dependent design changes and final confirmation are stopped pending those answers and the missing companion capability.

1. **Single-file row overflow:** The Goals say each file has at most 100 data rows, but D2 assigns the bound to the batch milestone and AC01 omits the row limit. With 101 entries that fit within 10 MiB and 30 seconds, what should `ledger export OUTPUT` do? **Recommendation:** retain the 100-row maximum and return an explicit overflow error rather than write 101 entries. Restricting the row bound to batch output changes the stated Goals. The failed destination's state is the separate question below.

2. **Failed single-file destination:** When a new single-file export reaches its size or time limit before all entries are written, should the destination retain a visible partial CSV, or should a CSV appear there only after successful completion? **Recommendation:** publish only a complete successful CSV and expressly permit cleanup of job-owned temporary output. This needs clarification of the broad “No ... deletion” boundary. Retaining a partial destination makes a normal retry fail the settled existing-destination refusal, so that choice also needs an explicit recovery contract.

3. **Batch crash between file and offset:** Suppose a numbered CSV is fully written, but the process stops before its completed row offset is durably recorded. May resume replace that unrecorded file, or must it recover the file as completed? **Recommendation:** define completion by a durable validated checkpoint and permit replacement of this run's uncommitted output, while preserving checkpointed files. Recovering an unrecorded file as complete requires durable evidence of its exact entries and offset. The current “partial file” wording does not settle this fully written, unrecorded case.

## Coverage and continuation

Actual coverage: source baseline; destination ownership; numeric-default change; single-file overflow and failure scenarios; one batch interruption boundary; observed milestone grouping and criterion references. This is scoped independent grounding, not a completed interview or artifact review. Input identity definition, input sourcing for the proposed CLI, concurrent writers, exact limit accounting, further recovery scenarios and complete acceptance/dependency semantics remain unreviewed. Supplied D1–D4 were retained as supplied decisions, not newly confirmed. No final shared-understanding confirmation was requested or recorded because material questions remain open.

Next action: answer the three frontier questions and make `author-rfc`, with its resolvable `implement-rfc` companion, available through the fixture's host discovery. Resume `grill-rfc` from `drafts/current/` and this continuation record; keep the supplied provenance and authored grouping. No install command is prescribed from an unavailable capability.

- `evaluation-result.md` — this account, capability limits, questions and continuation.
- `review-evidence/checks.json` — actual grounding results and input hashes.
